home.subtitle: Stone, light and trencadís. A place of silence and beauty open to everyone: pilgrims, neighbours and travellers.
home.crossQuote: "Carved in pale stone, this Crucifix stood beside the Pope in Barcelona."
home.crossP1: Today it rests beneath the trencadís arches — the mosaic of blue and golden ceramic shards that Catalan modernist masters raised like a broken and recomposed sky.
home.crossP2: It is the symbolic heart of the parish: the memory of a historic visit and a standing invitation to stillness.

historia.title: History
historia.lead: A hidden gem of Gràcia, raised by the community and cared for by volunteers.
historia.p1: The parish was born of the Vila de Gràcia neighbourhood, when local families joined forces to raise a church equal to their faith and their time.
historia.chapelTitle: The Chapel of the Blessed Sacrament
historia.chapelP: Designed by Francesc Berenguer i Mestres, Gaudí's right hand, the chapel gathers the best of Catalan modernism: parabolic arches, trencadís and light that shifts with the hours.
historia.gaudiTitle: Antoni Gaudí and his regular place of worship in Gràcia
historia.gaudiP: Gaudí lived and worked nearby, and this church was part of his everyday life of prayer. Walking its nave means following the architect's steps through the neighbourhood he loved.
historia.albertP: A group of neighbours, led by guide Albert, opens the doors of this architectural treasure so no one misses it.
historia.p2: The current church is the result of successive building campaigns. On its walls, the sobriety of stone, the goldwork of the altarpieces and the chromatic explosion of trencadís coexist — a technique where fragments of broken ceramic are recomposed into a new whole: a whole theology in tile.
historia.chapelP2: It is a space built for silent adoration, where architecture does not impress — it welcomes.
historia.guideP: Albert knows every stone of the church. His tours weave together neighbourhood history, Christian symbolism and modernist details easily missed by a distracted visitor.
historia.volunteerP: The initiative to keep the church open was born from parish volunteers: people who give their time so this architectural treasure never stays closed.
historia.conservationP: Every donation sustains the restoration of the stained glass, the mosaic and the organ. Preserving is also an act of hospitality.
